Quick Answer
You can edit Instagram Reels on Mac using Claude AI and the free Instagram Edits app. Install Claude Code, enable the app’s MCP automation server, and connect both. Then use simple text prompts to create projects, arrange clips, add transitions, titles, and effects, and export finished Reels in 4K.
The wait is over. The Instagram Edits app is finally available on desktop, but only on macOS, as of this guide. Instagram Edits is my go-to app not just for editing Instagram Reels, but also a reliable free video editor with all the features and a simple design.
Although the app is designed for creators and competes with CapCut, it has been limited to Android and iOS so far. But a few months ago, Instagram announced a desktop version, and now it is finally here. Right now, the app is only available on macOS, with Windows and other platforms coming in future releases.
I have been using the app for the past couple of days. It is very similar to the mobile app and is also free to use, but it also features an MCP connection, which you can use to connect to any of your AI subscriptions, such as Claude, Codex, and Muse, and let AI edit your videos.
The desktop interface is slightly different and can be complex for beginners. It took me a while to get used to it, but I have created a detailed guide to get started.
I also created a guide on how to connect your MCP, like Claude, to Instagram Edits to edit your videos, and it covers everything about this feature, including common setup errors. This guide is for beginners, so each step is comprehensive and detailed.
Table of Contents
How to Connect Claude AI to Instagram Edits and Edit Reels on Mac
Before connecting your Instagram Edits app to the MCP server, ensure you have the following pre-requirements:
- A Mac with an Apple chip (M1 or newer) on macOS 15.1 or later. Currently, the Instagram Edits desktop app is only available for macOS, with Windows and Linux versions coming soon, but there is no expected release date yet.
- Download and install the Instagram Edits app from here
- A paid AI subscription for any model; you can also use the free AI model.
Part 1: Get Claude Code
Step 1: Open Terminal and type the command: claude –version, and press Return. If you see a version number, it means Claude Code is already installed on your device. You can skip to Part 2 to continue setup.
If you see something like zsh: command not found: claude, it means Claude Code is not installed on your device, or Terminal can not find it yet. Follow the next steps to install Claude Code on your Mac.
Install Claude Code: To install Claude Code, use the official Anthropic installer. To do that, open Terminal on your Mac and paste this command: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
Wait a few minutes, and then you will see a ” Claude Code successfully installed message in your terminal.
Check the setup notes below. If you see something like installation exists but ~/.local/bin is not in your PATH, it means the terminal still can’t find Claude Code yet.
Now follow the next two steps. If you don’t see such a note, you can quit the terminal, reopen it, and use this command to confirm that Claude Code has been successfully installed on your device: confirm claude –version. If you see a Claude version, it’s installed on your device. Then continue with part two.
Next, paste this command into the terminal and press Enter: echo ‘export PATH=”$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH”‘ >> ~/.zshrc
Next, paste this: source ~/.zshrc, and press Enter. Now type claude –version and press Enter. You will see the Claude version number. This means Claude Code is successfully installed on your device in the terminal
Part 2: Turn on Claude access in Edits
Next, you need to let Claude access your Instagram edits apps. First, ensure the Instagram edits app is installed on your Mac. If not, you can use the official download link here. Once installed, follow the steps below:
Step 1: Open the app on your Mac and sign in with your account. On the home screen, you will go directly to the Projects tab.
Step 2: Next, you can tap on your profile picture in the top right corner of the screen or click on the edit option in the menu bar at the top of the screen and then click on the settings
Step 3: Next, tap on the automation from the sidebar
Step 4: By default, automation is turned off. Now, from the automation settings, turn on the toggle that says Enable Automation Server.
Step 5: Under the Connect an AI Client section, click the copy icon next to the Claude code. This will copy the connection command with your access token. Remember, don’t share this command with others. In this case, I am using Claude code. If you are using Codex, tap the copy button next to Codex. The same goes for Muse.
You can also connect any AI model. Since it is a standard MCP server, any AI app can connect to the MCP server over HTTPS and can control edits.
Remember to replace <TOKEN> with the Access token from Edits > Settings > Automation, and keep Edits open with the automation server turned on
For Google Gemini CLI:
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli
gemini mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp
For Qwen:
npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code
qwen mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp
For DeepSeek, Grok, Mistral, Kimi, GLM, and most others, we can use OpenCode
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
{
“$schema”: “https://opencode.ai/config.json”,
“mcp”: {
“servers”: {
“edits”: {
“type”: “remote”,
“url”: “http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp”,
“oauth”: false,
“headers”: { “Authorization”: “Bearer <TOKEN>” }
}
}
}
}
Part 3: Connect Claude Code to Edits
Next, let’s connect Claude Code (or any AI model) to edits. Remember that you can only do this once.
Step 1: Now, paste the command you copied from the previous section into the terminal. You will see: Added HTTP MCP server metapilot-native
Step 2: Next, for Claude, paste this command: claude mcp get metapilot-native and press Enter. Under status, if you see Connected, it worked. If it says Failed to connect, ensure the edits app is running and follow the previous steps carefully.
For other models, follow these:
| App (models) | Connect command | Check it worked | 
| Claude Code (Claude) | claude mcp add –transport http –scope user metapilot-native http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” | claude mcp get metapilot-native | 
| Gemini CLI (Gemini) | gemini mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp | gemini mcp list | 
| Qwen Code (Qwen) | qwen mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp | qwen mcp list | 
| Codex (OpenAI GPT) | echo ‘export EDITS_TOKEN=”<TOKEN>”‘ >> ~/.zshrc && source ~/.zshrc && codex mcp add edits –url http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp –bearer-token-env-var EDITS_TOKEN | Run codex, then type /mcp | 
| OpenCode (DeepSeek, Grok, Mistral, Kimi, GLM and more) | No command. Paste the opencode.jsonc block from my last message into the folder you run OpenCode in. | opencode mcp list | 
| LM Studio (local Llama, Gemma, Qwen, DeepSeek R1) | No command. Program tab, then Install, then Edit mcp.json, and paste the JSON block. | Look at the Program tab | 
| Cursor (any model it offers) | No command. Paste the same JSON into ~/.cursor/mcp.json. | Cursor Settings, then MCP | 
Part 4: Start Claude Code
Now go to the folder where the videos are saved to edit them using Instagram edits. I recommend that you store all the videos in the Movies folder so it is easy to access in the future. In this case, I stored all my files in the Movies folder on my Mac. Now, once you have access to the folder, follow the steps below.
Step 1: To use Claude, go to the folder using the CD command. For example: cd ~/Downloads or cd ~/Movies. In my case, cd ~/Movies. Next, once you are in the folder, Type Cluade and press Return.
Step 2: Claude will ask whether you trust the folder you provided. Use the down arrow and select I trust this folder, and press Enter. It asks only once, and once you give permission, you can store all future videos in this folder for edits.
Step 3: To check, you can type /mcp and press Enter. It lists the apps Claude Code is connected to. metapilot-native with a green tick means Claude can control Edits.
Step 4: Go to the metapilot-native option and press Enter to see more details. You can use the down or up arrow to navigate between the options.
Part 5: Make your first Reel with Claude
Now let’s use Claude to create my first reel. In this case, I asked Claude to edit a 50-second coffee reel from five clips. In your case, you can store all the clips in the folder. First, test the connection again. Once done, follow the steps below.
To test the connection, go to your folder and type list my Instagram edits projects and press Enter. You will see metabolist native and the table of all your edit projects.
Step 2 : Now you can ask Claude to make edits for the Instagram reel video. You can manually create a new project, add clips, and point Claude to the project title and edit your videos, or you can ask Claude to create a project, add clips, and edit your first reel. I recommend giving Claude the full location of your clips and the title.
Step 3: That’s it. Claude will now create a new project and add Sunclips. You can open the Instagram Edits app to see the changes.
Step 4: Once you’ve loaded the clips, you can ask Claude to add transitions between them and also add titles, sound effects, and much more. In this case, I’m asking Claude to add the title “Morning Coffee” in big white text for two seconds and then add smooth transitions between the clips.
Step 5: Once you’ve made the edits, you can also ask Claude Core to export the clips in 4K, and it does it for you.
Step 6: Once the video is exported, Claude notifies you of the length, format, and size. You can open the same folder to see the clip. Claude also notifies you where the clip is stored and its title.
Let AI Handle Your Video Editing
This is how to connect Claude code using Instagram Edits MCP. For now, the Instagram Edits app is only available on macOS, and you can connect any AI model to make edits.
Since Claude requires a subscription, you can try a free AI model if you have one. You can also run any free AI model locally and ask it to edit, but the quality may vary and may not be as good as frontend models.
Since this guide focuses entirely on Claude Code, we are also creating a separate guide on how to connect other free AI models, including Google Gemini (which comes with a free Jio AI offer), DeepSeek, and other models.
If you have any issues while connecting Claude Code, let me know. If you prefer a video guide, we have also created one that you can check out above.

US president Donald Trump arrived in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen on Wednesday to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, where he was received by Chinese President Xi Jinping at the airport.
He is also scheduled to hold a trilateral meeting with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump has said he intends to discuss limiting nuclear weapons and ending the war in Ukraine, which began in 2022 following Russia's invasion. However, his aides had earlier told reporters that the Ukraine conflict would not feature in the trilateral meeting.
The US president said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opportunity to resolve the conflict, expressing optimism about the prospects of an agreement.
“I think it’s very close to getting it done,” Trump said. “We’re going to have a good meeting on that.”
Trump also raised the possibility of a private meeting with Putin and a separate meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, although neither engagement has been confirmed.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio clarified on Wednesday that Trump was “serious” about meeting Kim to address tensions with North Korea. However, he indicated that no meeting between the two leaders had been scheduled for Thursday.
“I’m not telling you that there will be a meeting tomorrow,” Rubio said. “I’m just saying that" the president "is willing to meet and discuss, as he did during his first term.”
Trump's visit to China follows his participation in the Asean summit and the Quad leaders' meeting in Manila. Shortly before leaving the Philippines, he announced a new trade agreement with the country in a post on Truth Social.
"I am now heading to China, from the Philippines, where we had a wonderful meeting on Trade, National Security, and other subjects. I am pleased to announce that we made a new and completely different Trade Deal with the Philippines, one that will be a true landmark and, in particular, a Deal that will be great for our Farmers and those in the business of “Energy.” President Marcos is a powerful leader, and a man of high integrity and substance. It was an Honor to be with him, and his beautiful wife and son. See you in China."
Earlier on Wednesday, Putin held bilateral talks with Xi in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC forum, with both leaders emphasising the importance of strengthening Russia-China ties and advancing a multipolar world order.
Putin said the two countries must work towards shaping a fairer multipolar world, while describing their foreign policy relationship as stable and positive.
"Russia and China work to shape a fairer multipolar world order amid a challenging geopolitical situation. The Russian-Chinese foreign policy relationship remains stable and on a positive footing," Putin said.
Xi echoed the Russian leader's remarks, calling on both countries to take the lead in advancing multipolarisation and democratisation in international relations amid global uncertainty.
"We must firmly shoulder the responsibilities expected of major powers lead and advance the multipolarisation of the world and the democratisation of international relations," Xi said.
He also called for deeper cooperation across various sectors, saying the partnership had contributed to stability in an increasingly turbulent international environment.
"Our relationship has brought greater stability and certainity to a turbulent world."
Xi further described Russia-China relations as a model of equality, mutual respect and mutually beneficial cooperation.

CFTC tells Kalshi to stop letting people bet on Trump's speeches
The prediction market platform's CEO has complied but opposed the move.
On November 13, the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission ordered prediction market platform Kalshi to halt mention markets centered on President Donald Trump. The contracts in question were a "TRUMPSAY" series and one titled "What nicknames will Trump say before 2027?" These contract types allowed users to bet on whether the president would say particular words in a given time frame.
The CFTC wants to launch "a proceeding to determine whether Kalshi's certification that the contracts comply with the Commodity Exchange Act and the Commission's regulations was false." The prediction market has complied with the order, although Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour said he is opposed to pausing these bets.
The agency released a staff advisory on these predictions in September, noting that they "present a heightened risk of manipulation because their settlement turns on the discrete conduct of a person that may be neither independently generated nor externally verifiable."
Mention markets around presidential speeches, as well as predictions markets' possible ties to the current administration, have already stirred controversy. White House teleprompter operator Gabriel Perez was placed on administrative leave this summer after he reportedly made more than $100,000 betting on things that Trump would say. At that time, the CFTC said it would be willing to settle with Perez if he returned the money. Kalshi has also parted ways with Donald Trump Jr as one of its paid advisors; the move was dubbed a mutual decision based on Trump Jr's investment firm putting more funds into rival Polymarket.
The CFTC has mostly used a light touch in overseeing prediction markets, although the agency has been aggressive in staking its legal claim to be the sole regulator of these businesses. It has sued multiple states that tried to take prediction markets to court on charges that they constitute illegal gambling.

Bengaluru-based Recove Ventures has raised ₹56.3 Cr (slightly over $6 Mn) in a funding round from investors like Samara Capital’s CEO Sumeet Narang, Capri Global, Amit Prakash Sharma Family Trust, 5F World’s Ganesh Natarajan and Chaitanya Kejriwal (Parkson’s Packaging). Out of the total capital raise, ₹36.3 Cr came by way of equity allotment and the remaining is debt. The recycling startup plans to invest in spreading its infrastructure in Maharashtra and expand its footprint in Karnataka. The startup is targeting investments of over ₹2,000 Cr across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh over the next decade. It has signed 10-year MoUs with the governments of Maharashtra, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh, each involving proposed investments of more than ₹500 Cr. Founded in 2024 by Viral Chhajer, Kunal Kumar, Aayush Killa and Sharan Subaiah, Recove recycles plastic waste and sells it to companies that use such plastic to make new products. The startup claims to source its plastic waste from over 200 suppliers and sells its recycled plastic to over 40 customers. The startup is expanding across collection, segregation, washing and granulation. Its approach is to source and pre-process waste closer to where it is generated before moving it to larger facilities for further processing. It currently operates a washing facility at Harohalli in Bengaluru, which procures around 600 tonnes of plastic monthly as well as a pre-processing unit in Pune. Three more facilities are under development. Of this, a granulation plant at Maharashtra’s Jalgaon is expected to produce a monthly capacity of 1,100 tonnes. For context, granulation is the process of grinding plastic scrap into small, uniform pieces. The two year old startup sees a goldmine in waste plastic, claiming that billions of dollars worth recyclable plastic go to landfills each year in India. It sees a market opportunity of over $4 Bn up for grabs, and believes its organised supply chain infra could help save up a significant chunk of the $36 Bn plastic waste between 2025-30. However, the opportunity spans multiple waste streams, including electronic waste and metals, with businesses building solutions across collection, processing, material recovery and compliance. Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress announced the company’s Q3 earnings on Tuesday, without initially mentioning former CEO Jensen Huang or the details of his departure, or possible attempt at a return. On the earnings call accompanying the release, board chair Harvey Jones kicked things off by saying the board “does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO,” and that “we will not be addressing or taking questions on today’s call regarding the circumstances of Jensen’s resignation and the ongoing investigation,” before Kress started with her comments on the results.
Nvidia’s Q3 earnings hit the mark, without mentioning the whole Jensen Huang thing
Nvidia’s Q3 revenue has more than doubled, with income from data centers up 110 percent from last year, to $107.6 billion.
As it predicted in the last financial update, Nvidia is now on the list of companies that have pulled in over $100 billion in a single quarter, with revenues of $115.8 billion, up 103 percent from the same period last year and higher than its expectation of $108 billion. This quarter’s figures include data center revenues of $107.6 billion, which were up 110 percent, and edge computing (which includes the consumer gaming PC business and devices like the new RTX Spark laptops) revenue of $8.2 billion, up 42 percent.
The company reported $65.3 billion in profit, a new record.
“Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” said Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.”
In the fourth quarter, Nvidia expects revenues of $130 billion.

As rivals such as Netflix and Disney start encroaching on their world of creators, YouTube has returned fire with a new slate of programming from a slew of burgeoning creators such as Nick DiGiovanni and Emma Chamberlain, established stars including Phil Rosenthal and Aryna Sabalenka and one director that insiders have dubbed the “next Kane Parsons”.
The Google-owned streamer held its second annual Creator Premieres event at The Hollywood Roosevelt in Los Angeles, where it unveiled a raft of new titles.
DiGiovanni, who is behind the world’s largest food YouTube channel, is launching Chef. Chamberlain is launching What Are You Waiting For? Next year. The series, which comes from Amplify Pictures and exec producer Joe Lewis, sees the creator try to understand more about people who wait in line, particularly in New York.
Watch on Deadline
Last year, Saturday Night Live star Grace Reiter, who also stars on Netflix’s Minimum Wage, launched The Hunger Games (but better) parody. Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life.
To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts.
Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.
This year, Jarnecki has written about Iran’s drone and missile strikes on Amazon data centers in the Middle East during the US-Israeli war with Iran, and the broader implications for governments and Big Tech. He has also commented on the impacts of Russia and Ukraine exchanging strikes on each other’s data centers.

Scientists have assembled a cellular atlas of a crucial brain region called the basal ganglia involved in functions such as movement, decision making, emotions and habit formation — an accomplishment that could help guide new treatments for several devastating diseases.
The researchers mapped the cell types and cellular gene activity in the basal ganglia, an interconnected set of structures deep within the brain, in humans as well as in mice and in macaque and marmoset monkeys. Basal ganglia dysfunction is associated with conditions such as Parkinson’s disease, Huntington’s disease, schizophrenia, Tourette’s syndrome, bipolar disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder and addiction.
“It is important to understand the structure and function of the basal ganglia in order to develop effective treatments of these diseases,” said neuroscientist Hongkui Zeng, director of brain science at the Allen Institute in Seattle and one of the leaders of the research presented in more than two dozen studies published on Thursday in Cell and related journals.
“It is a major milestone in our journey toward a comprehensive, detailed, multimodal, cross-species aligned cell atlas for the entire human brain,” with a target date sometime in 2028, Zeng added.
The research was conducted as part of the BRAIN Initiative, an effort launched in 2014 to advance the understanding of the brain with the support of the US National Institutes of Health. The work presented on Thursday offers the first comprehensive cross-species cellular roadmap for any brain region.
“Until now, there was no reference describing each cell type in the human basal ganglia together with how it regulates its genes,” said Joseph Ecker, a molecular biologist and geneticist at the Salk Institute in La Jolla, California, another of the research leaders.
“In the near term, the atlas is a reference resource for researchers. We are studying a Parkinson’s gene and can now see which cell types turn that gene on, and which DNA switches are active in those cells. Over the longer term, the atlas can help identify cell-type-specific targets for gene therapy and gene editing,” Ecker said. “It also gives a baseline for comparing diseased tissue with healthy tissue.”
Therapies built on the new work are still years away, Ecker said.
Among other findings, researchers identified a new type of brain cell associated with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, documented genetic changes in specific cell types that could play a role in autism, and discovered changes in gene activity in certain cells associated with aging.
Cross-species comparisons
Using brain tissue from deceased human donors, the researchers examined the role of 21 million cells in the basal ganglia in people, as well as millions more cells in the three other species.
“Understanding the cellular composition of this brain structure across species will allow for comparative analyses of function as well as connectivity patterns and response to pharmacological interventions,” said Salk Institute neuroscientist and biochemist Margarita Behrens, another of the research leaders.
Many studies for ethical reasons cannot be performed using living human brains. Much of what was previously known about the basal ganglia, and most early testing of new treatments, had come from research involving mice and monkeys.
“We rely on animal models to probe the inner workings of brain cells and circuits in generating brain function and mediating disease effects, and to test the efficacies of therapeutic interventions,” Zeng said.
The structures of the basal ganglia include the striatum, globus pallidus and substantia nigra.
“Together they help select and start movements, and they support habit formation, reward learning, motivation and emotion,” Ecker said.
The atlas combines several layers of data. One shows which genes are switched on in each cell. Another involves the epigenome, a collection of chemical compounds and proteins that attach to the DNA and regulate gene activity. A third layer involves spatial maps showing where each cell type sits in the tissue of the basal ganglia.
“Most of the DNA variants linked to brain disorders lie outside the protein-coding parts of genes. Many of them sit in DNA ‘switches’ that control when and where genes turn on, and those switches are often active only in particular cell types,” Ecker said.
The protein-coding parts of genes carry genetic instructions used to build proteins, the complex molecules that perform most of the critical work inside cells.
An atlas like this one helps trace a disease-risk DNA variant to the specific kind of nerve cell or support cell where it acts.
“That is a first step toward understanding how the variant contributes to disease, and eventually toward treating it,” Ecker said.

- On Nov. 14, U.S. President Donald Trump shared on Truth Social what appeared to be a screenshot of a long post telling the story of how Trump allegedly once helped Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin's teenage son, who'd suffered a brain injury and could only remember the president.
- The post itself consists of AI-generated text and AI-generated photographs showing Trump hugging a teenage boy, with Mullin behind them in tears. Despite the artificiality of the post, it did track with a story actually told by Mullin during his confirmation hearing before a U.S. Senate committee on March 18.
- We found no reason to disbelieve Mullin's story, but we were not able to independently verify the details of it.
- We reached out to the Department of Homeland Security and the White House to learn more and will update this report should additional information surface.
In November, a rumor spread that U.S. President Donald Trump once helped Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin's teenage son, who'd suffered a brain injury and could only remember Trump. According the story, Trump called the young boy every day for two weeks.
Several Snopes readers emailed, asking us whether the story was true. They shared social media posts making the same claim, including from Facebook and Instagram. One Instagram post recounted a version of the story in detail in the caption and included images of Trump holding a teenage boy while Mullin cried (archived).
The caption read, in part:
Jim was a strong, gifted wrestler—his father's whole world—until a severe brain injury changed everything in an instant. When Jim opened his eyes, he didn't recognize his own parents. To the boy Markwayne had watched grow up every single day, his own father looked like a complete stranger.
According to Mullin's testimony, the only thing Jim still remembered was that Donald Trump was President.
When Trump found out, he didn't issue a press release or send a standard card. Mullin recounted how Trump personally called, sent his private plane to fly Jim to a rehabilitation center in California, and called the teenager every single day for two weeks while in the middle of a campaign.
Trump himself shared a screenshot of the story on Truth Social (archived), which he apparently took from an X user using the handle @GolfandTri:
(Truth Social user @realDonaldTrump)
The stilted style of the text and overly dramatic images suggested the entire post had been generated with artificial intelligence. We ran it through Pangram, an AI detector, which concluded that the images were AI-generated with near 100% certainty, as was the text, with 100% certainty. Snopes reached out to the X user whose post Trump shared to ask if they generated the text and images or found them elsewhere online.
Though the text and images were AI-generated, the tale appeared to have been inspired by a story Mullin himself told during his confirmation hearing before senators on March 18.
Though we found no reason to disbelieve Mullin's story, we couldn't independently confirm it, either. We reached out to the White House and the Department of Homeland Security seeking further details and we will update this report should we hear back. For now, we leave the claim unrated.
In the Senate hearing, Sen. Ron Johnson, a Republican from Wisconsin, asked Mullin why he was loyal to Trump. Mullin became emotional and recounted how the president had once helped his then-15-year-old son (the exchange starts at the 1:02:49 mark in this video):
The transcript of Mullin's response to the question read (emphasis ours):
Ron, I'm going to try getting through without crying then. It's not about President Trump, it's about my son. So, my son was a really world-class athlete, and Jan. 17 of 2020, which mind you was an election year, he had a really serious brain injury. Woke up 26 hours later and he was a different kid. We almost lost him. For 26 hours, he had extremely low pulse. There was a time that they thought that they lost his pulse altogether.
And when he woke up, he was just different. I mean, here you had a world-class athlete that wrestled all over the world since he was 12 years old and he couldn't touch his nose. He couldn't walk without shuffling his feet. He had short-term memory loss. And he couldn't control his muscles. Couldn't add five plus three. He was in high school at that time. Had to learn how to read, walk, everything.
And the president found out about it and he gave me a call immediately, and one thing that the president joked about was, he said, "Let me get this straight, he doesn't know who you and Chrissy are, but he knew who I was?" Because the only question he got right is who the President was, and he said, "Trump," with this cocky grin on his face. But the president didn't understand the severity of it, but he heard it in my voice and immediately he went to work. I told him we had to get to Bakersfield, California, to the Center for Neural Skills, which was one of the best neural rehabilitation places in the world. And the president offered us in his plane, his personal plane. This is president of the United States. And I said, "Sir, we can't fly. We got to drive."
We get there and he called almost every day for two weeks checking on Jim. And then he says, "I'm going to come see him." And now, this is the middle of the election. This is Bakersfield, California. Really not an area he's got to go campaign. And he took the time to come up there and see Jim. And the center told us that the short-term memory loss, something would trigger it. Some big event would eventually trigger where he'd start retaining stuff. Until then, he was still having issues. And the president arrived. And of course, there was cameras and everybody around. And of course, no one in media ever talked about it. Which was funny, because the president called him on stage and talked to him.
And then we went to the back, and the president didn't talk to me. He didn't know I was in there. He didn't even care if I was in the room. Here's a guy that's been over in his ties about as long as my son, because my son… It stunted his growth, and so he's 5'3" the rest of his life. And his team came to him twice and said, "Sir, we got to go. We got to go." On the third time they came over to him, he looked at them and he says, "Hey, I guarantee you that plane won't leave without me." And for the next 15 minutes, he did nothing but love on my son.
That one incident jogged his memory. And from then on, he started retaining things. And Jim's attitude went from this, you know, "We're going to get through it," to this, "I'm going to get through it." And every week, if not most days, the president would call and ask how he could help. Ask how's his buddy doing, "How's Jim doing?" He didn't do it for publicity.
Toward the end of his answer, Mullin became emotional again and used a tissue to dry his tears (around the 1:07:15 mark in the video). However, that image bore no resemblance to the AI images circulating online in November.
Snopes has examined rumors involving Mullin before, including the claim that the acquired Chevron and Raytheon stocks days before the U.S. military captured Venezuela's then-President Nicolás Maduro.

Environmental exposures during pregnancy and childhood, including tobacco smoke, indoor air pollution and dietary quality, may be associated with health outcomes such as BMI and behaviour, with many of these links persisting into adolescence, a new study has found.
Researchers, led by those at the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal), identified six prenatal and 42 childhood exposures associated with multiple outcomes and health families simultaneously.
The study, published in Science Advances, provides an atlas of associations between early-life environmental exposures and health, highlighting factors that may be relevant for prevention and policy action.
"Our approach allowed us to jointly analyse associations between the early-life exposome and multiple health outcomes instead of studying each one separately," first author Augusto Anguita-Ruiz, ISGlobal and University of Barcelona researcher, said.
The researchers used an outcome-wide exposome approach to study associations of exposures with health across four domains -- cardiometabolic, mental health, respiratory, and allergic problems.
The exposome refers to the totality of environmental exposures a person experiences throughout life, including factors such as diet, tobacco smoke and air pollution.
The exposures examined included diet, physical activity, sleep and other individual behaviours, as well as tobacco smoke, indoor and outdoor air pollution, chemical pollutants, metals and characteristics of the built environment.
The authors "identified a set of 'master regulator' exposures, such as maternal smoking, indoor air pollution, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, and dietary and urban factors, that influenced multiple health domains, with effects persisting into adolescence."
Senior co-author Valérie Siroux, researcher at the French National Institute for Health and Medical Research (Inserm), said: "Although no exposure was associated with all four domains, around one in three of the selected exposures was linked to more than one, suggesting that certain exposures can have broad and multisystemic effects on health."
Maternal smoking during pregnancy was associated with higher BMI and more externalising behaviours, such as aggression and impulsivity, in children during both early childhood and adolescence, as well as more ADHD symptoms during adolescence.
Higher maternal meat intake during pregnancy was also associated with several mental health outcomes and asthma in children, as well as wheezing and dermatitis during childhood.
Associations between environmental exposures and health parameters observed in early childhood were found to persist in adolescence.
The observation suggests that early environmental conditions may leave relatively durable health signatures, the researchers said.

Firaxis Games, the studio behind the Civilization and XCOM franchises of computer strategy games, last week laid off about a third of its staff, totaling around 60 people. That’s according to a recent report in Bloomberg.
The report cites people “familiar with the cuts,” saying that the flagship game the studio is currently working on, a new entry in the XCOM series, “has faced development struggles and missed a significant milestone.” The departures also include the studio head, Heather Hazen.
A Firaxis spokesperson released the following statement:
Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength—designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years. As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.
The storied studio has had a rough run of things of late. Its most recent game, Civilization VII, launched to solid enough sales but divided players in terms of reception. Players have long criticized new Civilization titles for being barebones compared to immediate predecessors that have seen multiple post-launch updates and expansions, but the response was sharper this time.

An easy way to free up storage on your Windows PC is to remove unnecessary apps — ones you no longer need. You identify the apps and delete them one by one. It’s pretty straightforward as long as you’re dealing with a couple of apps. If the number is higher, the method starts to feel tedious.
This is where a one-click uninstaller comes in handy, allowing you to delete multiple apps at once. Bulk Crap Uninstaller (BCU) is one such app. Here’s how it works and how to use it to bulk uninstall Windows apps on your PC.
What Is Bulk Crap Uninstaller, and What Makes It Better Than Other Tools?
Bulk Crap Uninstaller (also called BCUninstaller or BCU) is a bulk uninstaller that makes uninstalling multiple apps on your Windows PC at once incredibly easy. It can scan your computer comprehensively and find everything from Windows Store apps (pre-installed by Microsoft) and third-party apps to Steam games, portable apps, and Chocolatey packages. Bulk Crap Uninstaller stands out from other bulk uninstallers, including some paid alternatives, in a few ways. First, it can find broken or un-uninstallable programs and force uninstall them. Second, it can scan your file system and find leftover or orphaned items (files, folders, registry keys) left behind by apps you deleted manually. That way, you can safely and easily delete them and reclaim storage space. And third, it offers a “quiet uninstallation” mode that eliminates the need to click through dialog boxes and instead uninstalls the selected apps silently in the background.
How To Use Bulk Crap Uninstaller to Bulk Uninstall Windows Apps on Your PC
Bulk Crap Uninstaller is free to download and use. Go to the Bulk Crap Uninstaller website, and you’ll see multiple ways to download the app there. I recommend enabling the Select using checkboxes and Show items in groups options.

You’ll see additional details, such as size, version, publisher name, installation date, and certificate, next to each listing. You can use filters and sort options to filter out and sort items in a specific order.
Go through the list and tick the checkbox next to the apps you want to uninstall. The status bar at the bottom will show how many items you’ve selected and how much space deleting them will free up. Hit Continue while checking (and changing, if required) the settings, and click Begin Uninstallation.
You’ll see a prompt asking if you’d like to create a Restore Point. Select accordingly, and the app will uninstall the selected apps. While it deletes apps, you’ll see the uninstallation status in a dialog box. At any point, if you want to cancel the uninstallation, click the Cancel button.
Once Bulk Crap Uninstaller finishes uninstalling the selected apps, it will ask if you want to delete the leftovers too. Review the listed files carefully, uncheck the ones you don’t want to delete, and click the Delete selected button to get rid of them. Be sure to back up your registry if you’ll be deleting leftover registry keys.
When you uninstall apps this way, you’ll need to click through multiple dialog box menus to complete the uninstallation. Last but not least, Bulk Crap Uninstaller is highly configurable. As such, you can configure its behavior per your preference. Click the gear icon in the top toolbar to access the app’s settings. What I’m Not a Fan Of
I’ve used Bulk Crap Uninstaller on my PC for a while, and although it does its job well, there are a few aspects that I’m not a fan of and wish were better. Although rare, some users have complained about aggressive registry scanning, wherein Bulk Crap Uninstaller highlights shared keys (those used by other apps too) for removal. These aren’t drawbacks of Bulk Crap Uninstaller, though; they’re just a trade-off for its advanced capabilities. For this reason, it’s important to configure the app before you start using it and be completely sure about the actions you perform using it. You should also create a Restore Point when dealing with apps with broken uninstallers or stubborn leftovers. Trade talks between top Canada, U.S. officials ramping up: sources
No formal deal is on the table, work underway to reduce trade irritants
As talks with the Trump administration begin to ramp up once again, the prime minister's point man on Canada-U.S. trade has been meeting with his counterparts weekly in a more formal way, according to three senior government officials.
Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc has not travelled to Washington, D.C., to meet with U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer or Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick since talks restarted earlier this month. But there have been phone and video calls happening on a regular basis, the sources say.
Canada's chief trade negotiator Janice Charette is usually also on these calls, according to the officials.
CBC News is not naming the sources because they were not authorized to speak publicly about the trade talks.
The sources say while there is no formal deal on the table, both sides are working to remove trade irritants with the goal of eventually getting to one. Auto and steel tariffs remain key sticking points.
At this time, there are no plans for LeBlanc to travel to Washington for in-person talks, unlike over the summer, where both LeBlanc and Charette spent weeks working from the Canadian Embassy and met regularly at the U.S. trade representative's office.
But no deal was reached, and when talks fell apart the U.S. hit Canada with additional tariffs, prompting Canada to respond with countermeasures.
On Nov. 1, Prime Minister Mark Carney posted on social media saying teams from both countries would start working again on a trade deal.
"We all recognize that this period of trade uncertainty has created real challenges for Canadian businesses, workers, communities and of course the families of those affected," said LeBlanc at the international trade committee on Tuesday.
"We believe it is possible to make a deal that is, first and foremost, in the interest of Canada, but also in the interest of the United States, and ultimately also with our Mexican partners," he said in French.
The Advisory Committee on Canada-U.S. Economic Relations — a group of experts appointed by the federal government — are set to meet virtually on Thursday, where they are expected to discuss the situation on the ground in Washington and how financial support for tariff-affected industries is being implemented.
It will be the first meeting since the midterm elections, which saw the Trump administration lose control of Congress.
Democratic lawmakers have pledged to repeal tariffs on Canadian goods, although Democrats lack the two-thirds majorities in both chambers required to shield legislation from a presidential veto.
LeBlanc has said Canada's approach to finding a deal will not change despite the new political makeup of the U.S. Congress.
Goal is lowest tariffs possible: Charette
On Tuesday, Charette was asked by Conservative Canada-U.S. trade critic Shuvaloy Majumdar about whether Canada is now looking for a deal without tariffs.
"Madame Charette, you had suggested long-term tariffs are something we might have to accept. Would you say that tariff-free trade is now off the table, that's a decision the government has taken? Is the government's goal still tariff-free trade?"
Charette said the objective is to try to get as close as possible to tariff-free trade.
"I have suggested that we are trying to get to the lowest rate of tariffs on the narrowest basket of goods, with the most preferential access for Canadian businesses and Canadian workers," she said.
"But we do have another partner on the other side of the table and they have shown to date an unwillingness to enter into any arrangement in which there is full tariff-free trade."

Japan urges creation of an Asian energy framework to counter oil crises
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has proposed the creation of an Asian energy agency to help countries in the region cope with oil crises, such as the shocks from the Iran war
MANILA, Philippines -- Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi proposed Tuesday the creation of an Asian energy agency to help countries in the region cope with oil crises, such as the shocks from the Iran war.
Takaichi called for setting up an oil security task force and a Japan-based version of the International Energy Agency for the region. She put forward the plan at a meeting on the sidelines of the annual summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations in the Philippine capital, Manila.
“We would like to position this as an Asian version of the IEA,” Takaichi said.
The IEA is a multigovernmental but independent agency set up in 1974 in response to a severe oil crisis in the early 1970s. It provides policy recommendations and helps to coordinate oil reserves of its members. The Iran war that began in late February has raised the sense of urgency over energy security, especially in Asia.
Japan would help lead an Asian oil security task force, along with the Indonesia-based Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia, or ERIA, an energy security research organization, to develop rules for emergency releases and sharing of oil from national stockpiles, Takaichi told a meeting of the Asia Zero Emissions Community.
Japan is one of many Asian countries that depend heavily on imports of oil and gas. Takaichi's proposals follow a Japanese-led initiative announced in April to strengthen energy supply chains and cooperation in the region.
The region also should cooperate in stockpiling oil and set up a joint reserve system for Southeast Asia, Takaichi said. Idled oil storage tanks in Japan could be used for reserves, she said.
Soaring prices for oil and gas and disruptions to the shipping of oil from the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz due to the war led some countries in Asia to take emergency measures to conserve energy. It also has prompted a faster shift to use of renewable energy such as rooftop solar and electric vehicles.

Around one in five pregnant and lactating women in Assam’s Barak Valley and adjoining districts of Tripura suffer from suboptimal levels of ‘Thiamine’ (vitamin B1), according to a study by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN), Hyderabad, highlighting a continuing public health concern in the region.
The study, ‘Re-Emergence of Thiamine Deficiency Among Pregnant and Lactating Women in Northeast India’, published in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, examined the prevalence of thiamine deficiency and its link to dietary practices in areas where beriberi cases have previously been reported, said a press release on Monday.
Researchers conducted the community-based study during 2023-24 among 1,083 women from 120 villages in Assam’s Barak Valley and neighbouring parts of Tripura. Thiamine status was assessed using biochemical and functional indicators to determine the extent of deficiency.
The findings showed that about 20% of participants had inadequate thiamine levels. Based on blood thiamine measurements, 4.9% were deficient, and 15.2% had marginal levels. A separate functional assessment produced similar results, with 8.5% showing severe deficiency and 12.1% marginal deficiency. Pregnant women were found to be more vulnerable than lactating mothers.
Thiamine is an essential micronutrient that supports energy metabolism and healthy nervous system function. Deficiency can lead to serious health complications, making adequate intake particularly important during pregnancy and breastfeeding.
According to Mahesh Kumar Mummadi, NIN scientist and lead author of the study, dietary assessments revealed that most women consumed rice-based diets with limited diversity. Practices such as consuming stored rice, repeatedly washing rice before cooking, chewing betel nut and drinking salted tea were associated with a higher risk of deficiency.
NIN director Bharati Kulkarni said the findings underscore the need to look beyond routinely monitored nutrients in maternal health programmes. She called for greater dietary diversity, regular nutritional surveillance and targeted supplementation in high-risk regions. Researchers also noted that since the study focused on areas with previously reported beriberi clusters, the findings may not be representative of all pregnant and lactating women across India.

The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has warned of penal action against those failing to comply with the revised prices of 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs
The authority, which functions under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, has asked State drug controllers (SDCs) to strictly monitor the prices and submit their action taken reports by November 16, according to an official release on Friday (November 13, 2026).
The revised prices for the 137 anti-cancer drugs came into effect on November 9, 2026, following a gazette order issued on October 17, 2026. The order capped the trade margin on these medicines at 30%.
Based on submissions received from pharmaceutical companies up to November 11, the latest revised price lists have been uploaded on the NPPA website as well as the Pharma Sahi Daam app and portal, the Chemicals and Fertilizers Ministry said.
All manufacturers, stockists, dealers, retailers, hospitals, and medical institutions have been directed to comply with the revised prices and prominently display the updated price lists at their premises and on their websites.

Complaints regarding overcharging, shortage, or non-availability of medicines can be reported through the Pharma Sahi Daam app or portal, the NPPA helpline (1800-111-255), or via email at monitoring-nppa@gov.in, it added.

Maintaining physical and mental capacities is key to ensuring that older persons remain functionally independent. With age-related conditions such as visual and hearing impairment, memory and mobility issues often remaining undetected or unaddressed in the elderly, the National Centre of Ageing (NCA), Guindy has started to focus on providing integrated care to help older persons maintain functional ability. This is in line with the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) integrated care for older people approach (ICOPE).
According to the WHO, numerous physiological changes occur, and the risks of experiencing a decline in physical and mental capacities (intrinsic capacity) and having more than one condition (disease) increase when people age. This could manifest as cognitive decline, limited mobility, hearing loss, malnutrition, vision impairment, depressive symptoms, urinary incontinence and falls. ICOPE is WHO’s approach to provide a continuum of integrated care that helps to reorient health and social services towards more person-centred and coordinated care. It supports optimising intrinsic capacity and functional ability in older age, it said.

U.N. Starts Uncertain Effort to Regulate Lethal Autonomous Weapons
Delegates met in Geneva to discuss guardrails for such systems even as their development grows. Russia and the United States have resisted the efforts.
Global efforts to limit the use of lethal autonomous weapons reached a crossroads this week as countries gathered to decide whether to negotiate binding restrictions on the technology, despite strong resistance from the United States and Russia.
Delegates of 128 states met at the United Nations in Geneva on Monday for a weeklong conference to determine whether to draft a treaty that would ban lethal autonomous weapons and require meaningful human control of such systems.
“The longer the international community waits, the more difficult it will become to establish meaningful safeguards — and it may be too late,” Volker Türk, the U.N. human rights chief, said before the conference.
Artificial intelligence and its military uses are developing at breakneck speed, as seen on the battlefields of Ukraine and the Middle East. That has deepened international alarm and prompted calls for action by many countries, global leaders and activist groups, even as top military powers balk at attempts to curb their ability to develop new weapons.
“Decisions affecting human life, freedom and the use of force must always remain subject to effective, informed and responsible human oversight,” Pope Leo XIV said in a statement last month that urged those at the Geneva conference to take “concrete “steps” to ban lethal autonomous weapons. Artificial intelligence, he said, “must be ‘disarmed.’”
Russia and Ukraine have already deployed fully autonomous drones to carry out attacks. Disarmament experts fear that the low cost and easy availability of such technology could lead to its rapid spread to law enforcement, nonstate armed groups and organized crime.

The Karyavattom campus of Kerala University (KU) has emerged as a hotspot of dengue in the city, where over 50 cases have been reported since November 9. Health department suspects that this is a gross underestimation, as the transmission is likely to have begun weeks before
Intermittent spells of rain, followed by hot and humid weather, have led to the spike in dengue cases in Thiruvananthapuram, even when the general dengue case trend has been on a slow decline since July across the State.
In the last 10 days, Thiruvananthapuram district has reported 200 probable cases of dengue and 97 confirmed cases.
On Monday, following a meeting called by the Health department, which was joined by the Vice Chancellor, some KU syndicate members as well as public health experts of the School of Public Health under Kerala University of Health Sciences, it was decided to shut the Karyavattom campus and the hostel buildings for three days so that intense vector control measures can be taken up and a break in disease transmission can be achieved.
“District health officials and vector control teams had visited the campus and hostel and we found that solid waste management was a huge issue in the campus. Plastic disposable containers used for food delivery which are disposed of carelessly are emerging as a major contributor to vector breeding in urban areas.. Rain water stagnation in these containers which are strewn around is a major hazard. Indoor plants in hostel rooms, broken manholes and blocked drains leading to rainwater stagnation have all led to intense mosquito breeding inside the vast campus,” a senior Health official said.
The Health department has also decided to serve notice to the KU Registrar under the Kerala Public Health Act, for allowing the campus to be a breeding ground for mosquitoes and posing a public health issue
Teams from the Pangappara health centre have been at work on the campus since November 10 but the district vector control team and the Corporation health staff will be joining them now. Fogging will be done to kill adult mosquitoes and indoor space spraying inside the hostel room, which will be accompanied by a source reduction campaign, officials said.
The district health administration has identified several pockets of dengue within the city itself, where an abundance of breeding sources and intense vector breeding has been spotted
Health officials point out that several large government properties with vast, ill-maintained grounds are also turning out to be hotspots for dengue in the city.
“The Cliff House compound and the sprawling official bungalows around it are all major breeding grounds for mosquitoes. In the Cliff House, seven police personnel there on guard duty were down with dengue, following which a district health team had visited the location. In some of the bungalows where renovation works are going on, building materials and discarded parts of equipment are all thrown about carelessly, leading to rain water stagnation and mosquito breeding,” a health official said.
Health officials said that without public participation, source reduction and mosquito control cannot be taken up successfully.
Kollam district too has reported a significant number of dengue cases over the last 10 days.
In November so far, the State has recorded 739 confirmed cases and 2,056 probable cases of dengue and three probable dengue deaths.

Measles strategy works – Now it must expand to more countries
Cape Town Measles Declaration pledges to cut measles deaths by half
At a landmark World Health Organization (WHO)/United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) meeting in Cape Town, leading players in the fight against measles spelled out what it will take to stop 2000 children dying every day from this preventable disease. Together with UNICEF special ambassador Angelique Kidjo, they issued a call for intensified efforts and the resources necessary to ensure all children are protected against measles.
“We can do it – we’ve done it before – in Afghanistan, Angola, in countries devastated by conflict and drought and every other form of disaster,” said Carol Bellamy, Executive Director, UNICEF. “In just three years, and against great odds, we’ve cut the number of children dying from measles by almost 25%. It’s one of the most dramatic declines in disease mortality in history. But the next 25% will be harder. With the political and financial support of donors and governments around the world, we can together save many more lives.”
The “Cape Town Measles Declaration” calls on governments to take strong action against one of the world’s most vicious and prolific vaccine-preventable childhood killers – a disease which kills 745,000 children every year. We must control this disease to meet the Millennium Development targets of a 67% reduction in under-five mortality by 2015. The world leaders are well aware of the urgency. Last year, the UN General Assembly Special Session on Children set a 2005 target date to reduce measles deaths from 1999 levels by 50%. This year, the World Health Assembly, which includes 192 member states, endorsed the WHO and UNICEF measles strategy to combat the disease.
“When 30 million children are affected and 745,000 children die every year, you have to think big,” said Dr. LEE Jong-wook, Director-General of WHO. “Since the launch of the WHO-UNICEF strategy to reduce measles deaths in 2000, we have delivered measles vaccine to more than 200 million children globally. We know the strategy works. An additional half a million children are alive today because of all the partners’ efforts. But if we’re to prevent more deaths, we must do more. And we’ll need help from governments and from the international community.”
The campaign against measles has been dramatic – hundreds of thousands of children saved, the virus almost banished from the Americas and transmission cut drastically in many African countries, where the Measles Initiative Partnership has been the driving force behind the campaign. WHO and UNICEF have identified 45 countries as the highest priority for mortality-reduction strategies, accounting for 95% of global deaths from measles.
“It has been astonishing to see the results of the immunization programme in Africa,“ said Dr Mark Grabowsky, Senior Technical Officer, American Red Cross. “Now we have proof that we can reduce measles mortality even in countries torn apart by conflict, if governments are committed, communities are engaged and we have the support of donors, NGOs and volunteers. What we have accomplished so far through the Measles Initiative Partnership gives great hope for the future, and the many thousands of children we can still save.” The foundation of the measles mortality-reduction strategy is the re-invigoration of national immunization systems. At the Cape Town meeting, delegates discussed strategies with governments and policy makers for strengthening routine immunization services and making the life-saving measles vaccine available to all children as a matter of course.
”It’s not just about reducing childhood deaths today. We need to be in this for the long haul and this means a sustainable reduction in childhood deaths, which only a strong national health system can guarantee,” said Dr Stephen L. Cochi, Deputy Director, National Immunization Program, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). ”This kind of international focus and commitment gives us the opportunity to build that strength – boosting safe routine immunization services, establishing international laboratory networks and increasing surveillance to detect and respond to outbreaks.”
“Today the call to action is clear,” said Mr Nick Farrell, Senior Programme Officer, International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. “ We have to ensure every child receives a second opportunity for measles immunization in these 45 countries, no matter how remote or marginalized, regardless of barriers of conflict, culture and poverty.
“To date we have seen tens of thousands of health workers and volunteers trek across mountains and deserts in all kinds of conditions to find these children to ensure they receive the life-saving vaccine,” said Timothy E. Wirth, President of the United Nations Foundation. “We are witnessing incredible commitment from ordinary people. They need – they deserve to be backed up by the world’s political will and financial support.”
Ms Angelique Kidjo, Special UNICEF ambassador, believes that the Cape Town Measles Declaration indicates a clear path towards a giant achievement in children’s health.
”The world has committed, to drastically reducing the devastating, pointless waste of young life,” she said. “If we reach our targets for measles, we will have taken a huge step towards keeping that promise. I believe we can get there – but only if we make it a priority to turn this declaration into action. This goal deserves all we can give. We must do whatever is necessary.”
Further information:
- Of all the vaccine-preventable diseases, measles remains the leading childhood killer. Measles is an important cause of overall under 5 childhood mortality.
- Measles affects over 30 million children. More than 745,000 die each year from measles – more than half of them in Africa.
- A safe, effective and inexpensive measles vaccine has been available for over 40 years.
- Measles accounts for an estimated 50% of vaccine-preventable deaths among children.
- One million measles deaths are already being prevented each year with existing immunization efforts. With the successful implementation of the WHO-UNICEF measles strategy (including routine immunization and periodic supplementary immunization activities), an additional 500,000 measles deaths can be prevented each year.
- Measles is a highly contagious vaccine-preventable disease caused by the measles virus. It is one of the most readily transmitted communicable diseases and probably the best known and most deadly of all childhood illnesses. Measles causes a high fever, rash, cough and can kill. It affects mostly children, but also young adults. Children usually do not die directly of measles, but from its complications such as pneumonia and diarrhea which attack their weakened immune systems.
- It costs less than a dollar to immunize a child against measles.
- A critical goal is to reduce measles mortality by 50% by 2005 (compared to 875,000 deaths in 1999).
- The WHO-UNICEF strategy to reduce measles deaths includes: achieving and maintaining high routine measles immunization coverage – ‘the first opportunity’ to infants; Providing a ‘second opportunity’ for measles immunization for all children through periodic supplementary immunization campaigns; Ensuring high quality measles surveillance is in place to detect and respond to outbreaks; and improving management of complicated cases.
- Collaborating partners include: WHO, UNICEF, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the United Nations Foundation, humanitarian and non-governmental organizations, including the American Red Cross and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, governments of countries affected by measles, development banks, donor governments (e.g. Canada, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States of America).
- The importance of developing long term immunization planning cannot be underestimated. This includes ensuring measles activities are fully integrated with other national health goals, establishing high quality surveillance, mobilizing necessary human and financial resources and planning for financial sustainability of measles mortality reduction activities.

When you think of video editing, CapCut is a popular name that would pop up. It has made short-form editing painless. However, it has now started to put more of its tools behind a paywall, and a few of them need an internet connection to work.
If you are looking for a way out, you have probably already seen OpenReel, the browser-based open-source editor, or gone through our list of the best free video editing software. This time we have something different. Concat takes a different route. It is a free, open-source editor that runs on your own computer and is loaded with features like captions, voiceovers, and background removal built in.
Table of Contents
What is Concat?
Concat is a video editor that is currently in beta. The idea behind its development is easy to understand: It wants to give people stuff that CapCut offers but for free, like auto-captions, text-to-speech, background removal, keyframes, effects, titles, and 4K export. Everything Concat has on offer comes without strings attached. You don’t need to sign up, no watermark stamped on your exports, and no premium tier waiting around the corner.
The other big difference is where the work happens. Concat does everything locally, on your machine. It is built on a native Rust engine with a GPU compositor, and the AI models it uses (for captions, voices, and cutouts) are downloaded once from the settings and then run offline. This means the raw footage that you upload never gets uploaded anywhere.
CapCut is still a great editor, and nobody is pretending otherwise. When we compared it with Instagram Edits, we pointed out that CapCut has the richer feature set, but also that some of its tools need a connection and that its template and music ecosystem is tied closely to TikTok, which owns it. And if you are in India, you already know CapCut is banned here. So, you have to download the modded version or depend on some ad-filled alternatives.
That is the gap Concat is trying to fill. Not a “lite” version of a big editor, but a free one that keeps the stuff you reach for every day and keeps it on your own PC.
Concat features that matter
The feature list is long. But here are the parts that stand out.
Auto-captions that work offline
Captions are quite important nowadays, as content is reaching every part of the globe. But it is a chore every Reels and Shorts editor knows too well. Concat handles them using Whisper, a speech-recognition model that runs locally. You pick a model size (you can choose larger models, which are more accurate but require a stronger machine), and styled captions appear straight on your timeline. No upload, no waiting on a server, and it keeps working without internet.
Text-to-speech and voice cloning
Concat gives you free voices for narration, which is handy for tutorials or faceless channels. You can also clone a voice from just a few seconds of recording. That’s nice to edit a flubbed line without re-recording a whole take.
Background removal
You might have removed people or objects from your images. For videos, most of the editors ask you to pay. But Concat lets you edit out people or objects from a clip for free. If the automatic cutout misses a spot, you can paint the mask manually.
Keyframes with a curve editor
With keyframes, you can animate almost anything over time: position, scale, rotation, opacity, volume, and the settings of effects. There is a built-in curve editor too. You can use this to make a zoom feel smooth instead of mechanical, something that a paid video editor offers.
100 effects, filters and transitions
Concat comes with about 100 effects, filters, and transitions. They are rendered by your GPU and show up live in the preview. This way you can see what you are doing instead of waiting for an export to find out.
Fast cutting and a proper timeline
You get everything like split, trim, ripple delete, merge, freeze frame, and speed changes. If you like clips snapping together without gaps, you can switch on a magnetic timeline. Additionally, you can stack as many tracks as you want for overlays and picture-in-picture, keep several timelines inside a single project, and use blend modes like screen, add, and multiply. Crop and flip tools are there as well.
Titles with real styling
You can change fonts, add strokes and shadows, and drop in a background plate behind the words. If you don’t have any ideas, you can start from the already available presets.
One-switch audio cleanup
If your video has bad audio because of a faulty microphone or nearby noise, it can spoil a good video more than bad lighting does. Concat has a simple toggle for noise reduction, voice enhancement, and loudness leveling. You can also change voice effects to chipmunk, robot, and telephone.
Export and performance
Now, the best part is that with Concat, there is no limitation on export. It supports H.264, HEVC, and AV1, up to 4K at 60 frames per second with 10-bit colour.
Which platforms does Concat support?
Concat is versatile and supports multiple operating systems:
- Windows
- macOS
- Linux
- Android
- iPhone and iPad
Moreover, the editor is available in 26 languages. Downloading and setting up Concat is simple. Here’s what you need to do:
- Open the official download page, which picks the right build for your device. You can also grab any version from the GitHub Releases page.
- Install it like any other app on your device.
- On Windows, your system may warn you because the builds are not code-signed yet. Click More info, then Run anyway.
- On macOS, if the system refuses to open the app, the project suggests running xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Concat.app in Terminal.
- Open Settings and download the AI models you want (captions, voices, cutout). After that, they work offline.
Concat vs CapCut
| Feature | Concat | CapCut | 
|---|---|---|
| Price | Free, no subscription | Freemium | 
| Who is behind it | Open-source project (AGPL-3.0) | ByteDance | 
| Internet needed | Only to download AI models once | Some tools need a connection | 
| Templates and music | Limited | Large library tied to TikTok | 
A few things to keep in mind
Concat is promising and has all the features you would need from a video editor that is trying to be an alternative to CapCut. But don’t forget that it is young, and there are a few caveats that you should know about.
- It is a beta. The repo had over 200 open issues at the time of writing this article. So, you may come across some rough edges. We would advise you not to trust it with a client deadline until you have tested it on your own projects.
- Unsigned Windows builds and the macOS quarantine step can feel sketchy to newcomers. But it is safe, even though they are expected for now.
- You do not get a stock library to lean on. You will need your own assets.
- iPhone users have extra work because you have to sideload it, and sideloading is not for everyone.
Once you have the clarity, you should give Concat a try and let its output help you decide if you should keep using it or not. Let us know in the comments below which editor you are currently using.

People with diabetes could be at a 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's disease, compared to those living without the metabolic disorder, a review of studies has found.
Researchers, led by those from Australia's Curtin University, conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 studies. They found that if 1,000 people living with type 2 diabetes were followed for a year, an estimaated average of 4.7 would develop Alzheimer's disease, a neurodegenerative disorder in which memory and thought processes steadily decline with age.
Cognitive risk prevention should be integrated into diabetes care, they said.
"Individuals with T2D (type 2 diabetes) experienced approximately five AD (Alzheimer's disease) cases per 1,000 person-years and a 53 per cent higher risk of AD, supporting the rationale for integrating cognitive risk prevention into diabetes care," the authors wrote in the study published in the journal Alzheimer's Research and Therapy.
Study author Emmanuel Adewuyi, an investigator fellow at Curtin University's school of population health, said the review was important as it quantifies the relative risk and incidence of Alzheimer's in people living with type 2 diabetes.
"While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred," Adewuyi said.
"Relative risk tells us how two groups compare, while incidence tells us how often new cases occur: putting those numbers together gives us a clearer picture of the burden of Alzheimer's disease among people living with type 2 diabetes," the author said.
Databases including MEDLINE, CINAHL and Embase were searched from for publications since inception until April 2026. Forty studies, involving 27,102,559 data points, and looking at the incidence of Alzheimer's disease among people with diabetes or link between the two disorders were analysed.
